governed_construct: A named object-type definition: every `interface` declaration, and every `type` alias declaration (top-level or local, exported or not, generic or not) whose aliased type is an object type literal `{ ... }` (possibly parenthesized).
interpretation: The rule asks that named object shapes be declared with `interface` rather than `type X = { ... }`. An interface declaration is a conforming instance; a type alias whose right-hand side is directly an object type literal is a non-conforming instance. A union of object literals (e.g. `type R = {a} | {b}`) is treated as an object definition expressed with `type` and counts as a violation, since each member is an inline object definition that could be an interface. Type aliases that are not object definitions (string/literal unions, function types, utility-type references such as Record<...>, keyof, mapped or conditional types) are not instances and are neither conforming nor violating. Inline object types in annotations (e.g. a parameter typed `{ x: number }`) and object literals in values are not definitions and are ignored. Text in comments and strings is ignored. A file with no interface and no object-literal type alias is NOT_APPLICABLE.
